title: Common endophyte network resource-exchange study

publication.citation: Waschk et al., Resource exchange through common endophyte networks formed by non-mycorrhizal fungi, Scientific Reports, 8 June 2026

study_profile.system: controlled triple-compartment Petri dish / common endophyte network
study_profile.treatment_notes: isotope-labelled nutrient / carbon assays under study-specific compartment conditions

admission_gaps: verify exact GitLab revision and archive file inventory
verify data and script licensing separately from article licence
verify isotope label identity, source compartment and assay units for every raw file
preserve replicate, treatment, timepoint and destructive-sampling identity
record damaged or excluded samples and the exact endpoint affected
map all hypha-permissive / hypha-exclusion / plant-presence / isotope-control arms
retain missing donorless and isotope controls as design limitations rather than imputing them
assess the reported D2O abiotic-transfer signal as a competing explanation
do not merge 13C and 15N into a common scalar exchange measure
distinguish direct fungal transfer, microbial mediation, diffusion and contamination hypotheses
reproduction_requirements: reproduce one paper figure or table from the exact admitted data and scripts
report each isotope and compartment separately
run a control completeness audit before causal transfer attribution
preserve per-replicate data and uncertainty; do not only transcribe treatment means
state where the experiment cannot identify direct hyphal-mediated transfer
do not infer universal transfer coefficients or field-scale rates
claim_ceiling: The paper is a controlled study involving the named host and non-mycorrhizal fungal isolates. Its isotope findings do not by themselves establish general endophyte network transfer, direct fungal causation, field ecosystem rates, or a universal parameter. No source bytes have been admitted by this manifest.
